clue.text: This contest will be a close one

definitions.text: This contest will be a close one

parts.words: This contest will be a close one
parts.note: close reads as tight or evenly matched, but the contest is literally close, fought at arm's length with no weapons between the fighters

explanation.surface: A pundit predicts a tight match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' suggests a narrow margin of victory; it really means physically near, as in a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl fought with fists at very short range is a contest where the opponents are physically near each other.

clue.text: Important arbiters -Wimbledon umpires?

explanation.surface: Officials at the famous tennis tournament are described as weighty decision makers.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; the umpire sits in a high chair beside the court, hence the whimsical second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior judges of the superior courts are important arbiters; jokingly, the umpires at Wimbledon officiate on lofty tennis courts.

clue.text: Hastened up with speed to tell the tale

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for hastened is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: hastened means ran
speed means rate, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to tell a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'to' are links; 'Hastened up' reads as hurried along, but in a down entry 'up' means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to tell the tale; it is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Bound to be drawn

explanation.surface: Something is certain to be sketched or pulled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to be' reads as 'sure to be', but 'Bound' is a definition on its own; a drawn game is a tied one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied means fastened with rope, and also level at the end of a match with neither side winning.

clue.text: Finding cannabis will settle his hash

indicators.note: settle his hash is an idiom for dealing with someone, but here settle means the letters of his hash are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police who find drugs will deal with the offender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle his hash' is an idiom for putting someone in their place; the anagram of HISHASH is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hashish is a resin drug made from the cannabis plant.

clue.text: It sounds bad lacking love-but they're in the pink!

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters that follow are mangled into a new order
lacking means the zero for love is taken out of the word sounds

parts.note: love means nil in tennis scoring, so the letter O

explanation.surface: Something seems wrong without affection, yet these people are healthy and happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes O from SOUNDS to leave SUNDS; 'bad' rearranges IT + SUNDS. 'In the pink' usually means in good health; here it means showing bare pink skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists go about naked, so their bare skin is on show; the phrase is a jokey stand-in for unclothed people.

clue.text: Lent, for example, at an exorbitant rate

explanation.surface: Money was lent out at very high interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lent' looks like the past tense of lend, matching 'exorbitant rate' as interest; it is the Christian season of abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: Lent is a period of abstaining from food, a fast; fast also means quickly, at a high speed.

clue.text: Permission to start?

parts.note: a signal giving approval to begin, phrased as an instruction to set off moving forward

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they may begin.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyphenated noun meaning authorisation to proceed, as in getting the nod for a project.

clue.text: People pop inside where they see this sign

definitions.text: People pop inside where they see this sign

parts.words: People pop inside where they see this sign
parts.note: pop seems to mean drop in briefly, but it is slang for pawning goods, so the sign marks a pawnbroker's shop

explanation.surface: Shoppers nip in when they spot a particular shop sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' is British slang for pawn; three golden balls hang outside a pawnshop as its traditional emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional emblem hung outside a pawnbroker's shop, where people pawn possessions for loans.

clue.text: Gems that may appear strange in a new setting

indicators.note: a gem in a new setting suggests jewellery, but here the letters of strange are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: Jewels might look odd once mounted differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' plays on a jeweller's mount while signalling the rearrangement of STRANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Garnets are deep red semi-precious stones, so they are examples of gems.

clue.text: The padre is sunk in gloom

indicators.note: sunk suggests deep sadness, but here it signals the letters of padre is are wrecked and reformed

explanation.surface: The chaplain is deeply depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sunk in gloom' reads as one phrase; 'sunk' is the anagram signal and 'gloom' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is utter hopelessness, a deep form of gloom.

clue.text: A meeting of hands express approval

explanation.surface: A handshake or a show of hands signals agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A meeting of hands' suggests a gathering of workers; it is palms striking each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A clap is the striking together of palms, and to clap is to applaud.

clue.text: Climbing gear?

parts.note: seems to mean ropes and harnesses for mountaineers, but means the low car gear used for going up steep hills

explanation.surface: A question about mountaineering equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Gear for climbing suggests equipment; a driver selects the lowest gear to climb a steep slope.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest gear on a car gives the most pulling power, so drivers use it on steep inclines.

clue.text: Dole out food, say?

indicators.note: say means the word for food is spoken rather than written

parts.note: food here means meat, the flesh of animals eaten

explanation.surface: Someone hands out rations.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to distribute or allot, the same as to dole out.

clue.text: Boat with half the crew in the stern

indicators.note: half means only the first two of the four letters of crew are used

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship, which sailors call aft

explanation.surface: A vessel has some of its sailors at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the' joins the pieces; AFT is the nautical word for the rear of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft is a general word for any vessel or ship.

clue.text: Part of prison circle in large-scale fiddle

parts.note: a prison is divided into cells where inmates are kept
a circle is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A prisoner's scam in a jail is a big swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' suggests a swindle beside 'prison'; it is a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a big member of the violin family, and fiddle is an informal word for violin.

clue.text: Find made by a hunter

indicators.note: made by means the letters of a hunter are worked into something new

explanation.surface: A huntsman makes a discovery.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something is to dig it up, to discover or locate it.

clue.text: Profligate poet?

explanation.surface: A wasteful writer of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Spender (1909-1995) was an English poet of the 1930s generation alongside Auden.
explanation.definitionFit: A spendthrift wastes money freely; Stephen Spender was a twentieth-century English poet.

clue.text: Deal in cars

explanation.surface: Someone buys and sells motor vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal in cars' reads as a car dealer's trade; split it after 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To traffic is to trade, especially illegally; traffic is also the vehicles moving on roads.

clue.text: A musical term, and a type of bet

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up before cards are dealt in poker

explanation.surface: A list gives a piece of music jargon and a gambling word.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the Italian direction to play at a moderate walking pace.

clue.text: Continue to flirt?

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to keep up a dalliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry on with' someone is an idiom for having a fling.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is to keep going; it also means to have an affair or behave flirtatiously with someone.

clue.text: Being hardened, a summons is nothing to us

parts.note: a summons is a call, as in being called to court
nothing means zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone tough shrugs off an official demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Callous means insensitive and unfeeling, as of skin or a heart grown hard.

clue.text: Top-quality work produced by pupils in college, initially

parts.note: a group of pupils taught together is a class

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each of the words in and college

explanation.surface: Excellent work done by students at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' picks the first letters of 'in college', giving IC.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a work of lasting excellence, a model of its kind.

clue.text: Moves at first chance

explanation.surface: Early movements create an opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess sense: the standard series of moves at the start of a game is the opening.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess an opening is the set sequence of first moves; an opening is also an opportunity.

clue.text: Prepare for take-off?

parts.note: seems to describe an aircraft readying for flight, but means unfastening clothes before removing them

explanation.surface: A pilot readies a plane for departure.
explanation.walkthrough: Take-off suggests aviation; you unfasten buttons or zips before taking a garment off.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten buttons or a zip is a step before removing clothing.

clue.text: Interrupt a rest period

explanation.surface: Someone cuts into a pause from work.
explanation.definitionFit: To break in is to interrupt; a break is a pause or interval from work.

clue.text: Some passer-by from Belgrade?

indicators.note: some means only part of the word passer-by is taken, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A pedestrian from the capital of Serbia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks letters from inside 'passer-by'; Belgrade is the capital of Serbia, so the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Serbia, whose capital is Belgrade.

clue.text: Exchange of prisoners of war coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the abbreviation is read from bottom to top

parts.note: POWs is the standard abbreviation for prisoners of war

explanation.surface: Captives are traded as an exchange is arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns POWS into SWOP, a variant spelling of swap.
explanation.definitionFit: A swop, a variant spelling of swap, is a trade of one thing for another.

clue.text: Items given for storage in a bank?

definitions.text: Items given for storage in a bank?

parts.words: Items given for storage in a bank?
parts.note: a bank suggests money deposits, but a computer store of information is meant, holding facts and figures

explanation.surface: Valuables are lodged in a bank vault.
explanation.walkthrough: The bank is a computer memory store of information, not a financial institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and figures are what a computer information bank stores.

clue.text: Passage shows the band has style

parts.note: a band of people is a gang
a style or manner is a way of doing things

explanation.surface: A music group shows flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' hints at musicians; it is a group, a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangway is an aisle or walkway between rows of seats or onto a ship.

clue.text: Leaps in, disturbing the dog

indicators.note: disturbing means the letters of leaps in are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Something jumps in and upsets a hound.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is a breed of gun dog with long drooping ears.

clue.text: A new broom often makes them

definitions.text: A new broom often makes them

parts.words: A new broom often makes them
parts.note: from the proverb that a new broom sweeps clean: a fresh manager brings in far-reaching reforms

explanation.surface: A newly appointed boss reorganises everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A new broom' is an idiom for a newcomer in charge eager to reform; the brushing motion of a broom completes the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Far-reaching reforms are what a new person in charge introduces, sweeping away the old ways.
